page: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 236 GB, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this server type.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU execution, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded scaling present a clear tradeoff. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core score, and PassMark CPU score fall into the average category, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang drop to the weak tier. Memory bandwidth for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks remains in the average range, as do Redis SET operations and PassMark database operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F2amds_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated AMD EPYC cores, making it a resource-dense option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallelization. The server is suited for single-threaded processing tasks, text processing, and lightweight database operations. Conversely, it is less suited for highly parallelized workloads, software compilation, ray tracing, or medium-to-large language model inference, where benchmarks show weak to poor performance.
